name: J.C.R. Licklider

summary.text: J.C.R. Licklider was a psychologist and computer scientist who in 1962 became the first head of ARPA's computer research programme, which he named the Information Processing Techniques Office (IPTO). In 1962–63 he circulated memos describing an 'Intergalactic Computer Network', a concept that influenced the later ARPANET. He left IPTO in 1963–64; his successors Ivan Sutherland and Robert Taylor funded the ARPANET, managed by Larry Roberts.

facts.claim: Licklider was the first head of ARPA's computer research programme, which he called the Information Processing Techniques Office, and wrote about his 'Intergalactic Network' concept in 1962.
facts.quote: Licklider was the first head of ARPA's computer research program, which he called the Information Processing Techniques Office

facts.claim: A 1963 Licklider memorandum was addressed to the 'Members and Affiliates of the Intergalactic Computer Network'.
facts.quote: members and affiliates of the Intergalactic Computer Network

facts.claim: Sources differ on Licklider's IPTO tenure: one gives 1962–1964, another says he left IPTO in 1963 to run ARPA's behavioural sciences and command-and-control work.
Robert Taylor, who became IPTO director after Licklider and Ivan Sutherland, decided in 1966 that the time was right for a network and is credited with funding the ARPANET project.
facts.quote: it wasn't until 1966 that he decided the time was right for a network

connections.claim: Licklider headed ARPA's Information Processing Techniques Office from 1962.
Roberts, who managed the ARPANET project at IPTO, was influenced by Licklider's network concept.

openQuestions: The site's 'DARPA Node 0' entry dates the IPTO story to 1971; Licklider's first IPTO tenure was 1962–64 (he returned in 1974–75). The owner should check which period the page means.
